blocks.raw:
<Tip>**Three Indian architectural traditions—testable distinctions:**

**Hindu temples:** Shikhara tower above garbhagriha sanctum. North Indian (Nagara): shikhara-dominant, dense sculpture. South Indian (Dravidian): gopura-dominant, gopura gateways, vast walled precincts.

**Buddhist stupas:** Hemispherical dome encasing relics. Pradakshina (clockwise circumambulation) as worship. Sanctum inaccessible; relic presence spiritual, not visual.

**Mughal monuments:** Chahar bagh (4-part garden), domed chambers, pietra dura inlay (colored stone), symmetrical axes. Example: Taj Mahal.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <Note>North Indian (Nagara) vs. South Indian (Dravidian) temple distinction is LEA-tested: Nagara temples are shikhara-dominant (tall tower above sanctum), feature corbeled arches, and dense sculptural programs. Dravidian temples are gopura-dominant (massive gateway towers), feature mandapa columned halls, and emphasize large walled precincts. Understanding this regional typology prevents conflating distinct traditions and demonstrates regional-chronological knowledge.</Note>

blocks.raw: <Warn>Do not confuse shikhara (Hindu temple tower above sanctum) with gopura (monumental gateway tower, especially in South Indian temples). Shikhara is cosmic-spiritual symbolism; gopura is administrative entrance marker. Both are vertical, but their functions and placement differ fundamentally. Similarly, do not treat stupas as interchangeable with temples: stupas are Buddhist, house relics, and emphasize circumambulation; temples are Hindu, house deities, and emphasize axial entry. These distinctions are directly tested on the LEA.</Warn>

blocks.children_raw: Do not confuse shikhara (Hindu temple tower above sanctum) with gopura (monumental gateway tower, especially in South Indian temples). Shikhara is cosmic-spiritual symbolism; gopura is administrative entrance marker. Both are vertical, but their functions and placement differ fundamentally. Similarly, do not treat stupas as interchangeable with temples: stupas are Buddhist, house relics, and emphasize circumambulation; temples are Hindu, house deities, and emphasize axial entry. These distinctions are directly tested on the LEA.
